title: How AI assistants choose what to recommend

blocks.text: More and more people ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Claude "what is the best app for…" instead of searching Google. AIO (AI optimization) is the work of making those assistants name your product — and describe it correctly.
Where the answers come from

items: Memory: what the model learned from the internet when it was trained — mostly well-known brands and pages that were written about a lot. It changes slowly (months).

Web search: ChatGPT with search, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews search the web in the moment and build the answer from the pages they find. These pages are cited as sources — and you can get into them in weeks.

Repetition: a product that appears in many lists, reviews, comparisons and forum threads is "the obvious answer". One great page on your own site is not enough; you need to be mentioned around the web.

blocks.text: What Seenlab does on this page

items.title: Asks
items.text: On each assistant’s day it asks the questions your customers ask, the way a person would.

items.title: Reads
items.text: It finds whether you are mentioned, in which place, who is recommended instead, in what tone, and what is claimed about you.

items.title: Shows the way in
items.text: It lists the pages the assistants cite when they recommend others, writes the pitch for each and the pages worth publishing on your site.

items.title: Measures
items.text: Every change you log is compared before and after, so you see what really moves the answers.

blocks.text: The plan tab shows the AI-visibility actions from the morning plan: a lost mention to win back, a wrong claim to correct, a page the assistants cite that you should get into, a comparison page to publish. Each has the reason, the steps and a ready draft.
The same plan also has SEO actions — they are on the SEO page. Both are written in one go — every morning on Pro, on Mondays on Free.

A prompt is a question a customer would ask an assistant. Seenlab asks each prompt to every connected assistant on that assistant’s day. A project tracks 2 prompts on Free, 15 on Pro and 50 on Studio, so choose the ones that matter most.

items: Write them like a customer, not like a marketer: "what is the best habit tracker with a widget" rather than "Habitloom features".
Cover different intents: "best X for Y", "alternatives to <competitor>", "X vs Y", "how do I <problem your product solves>".
Use the language and the country of your customers.
Do not put your own brand in the prompt — then you measure nothing.

items.label: Suggest
items.text: The AI proposes prompts from your product and competitors.

items.label: From searches
items.text: Questions people really type on Google that bring your site impressions (from Search Console). Real demand is the best source.

items.label: Mentioned in
items.text: The share of answers that name your product. The main number to move.

items.label: Share of voice
items.text: Of all products named across the answers, the share that is yours. It shows how much space you take compared with competitors.

items.label: Average place
items.text: Where you are among the products an answer lists, when you are mentioned. First place is what people pick.

items.label: Most mentioned
items.text: The competitor the assistants name most often — usually the one to study first.

blocks.text: Answers vary: the same question asked twice can give different lists. That is why trends over days matter more than one answer. When samples are on (asking each prompt more than once a day), the mention rate per prompt is a percentage of those samples.
A daily rate that jumps between 0% and 100% for one prompt means you are "on the edge": a few more mentions around the web usually make it stable.

blocks.text: Assistants that search the web give sources — that is where the Sources and "where to be" lists come from. Memory-only assistants change slowly; they follow what the web says about you over months.
Each assistant is turned on when its API key is set on the server. Every answer costs a little, which is why the number of prompts is limited for now.

"Where to be" lists the pages the assistants cite in answers that recommend your competitors and not you: "best tools" articles, review sites, directories, forum threads. Getting onto these pages is the fastest way into the answers, because the assistants already trust them.

items.title: Start with the pages cited for several prompts
items.text: They are sorted by how many of your prompts they appear in.

items.title: Press "Write the pitch"
items.text: Seenlab reads the page and writes what fits it: a short email to the author of an article, an honest reply for a forum thread, or what to submit on a directory.

items.title: Send it personally
items.text: Adjust the draft, send it from your own address, follow up once after a week.

items.title: Log it
items.text: When you get in, add an experiment in the Changes tab to see the effect on the answers.

blocks.text: On forums (Reddit and others) always say you are the founder. Hidden self-promotion gets removed and hurts the brand more than it helps.

Being mentioned is not enough if the assistant says something wrong: an old price, a platform you don’t support, a missing feature. Seenlab checks every statement an answer makes about your product against your product facts and marks it correct, wrong or unclear.

items.title: Write your facts
items.text: On the Product page: price and plans, platforms, main features, who it is for. The more precise, the better the check.

items.title: Fix the source, not the answer
items.text: Wrong claims come from old articles, reviews and your own outdated pages. Update your pricing page and FAQ, add schema, and ask the cited pages to correct it.

items.title: Compare the picture
items.text: "How AI describes you" shows the one-sentence picture each assistant has of you, next to how you want to be described. If they differ, your site and the pages about you say something else than you think.

blocks.text: Write your positioning as one sentence a customer would repeat: "the simplest habit tracker for busy people". Then say it the same way on the home page, in the store listing and in every pitch.

Assistants love to cite three kinds of pages: comparisons ("A vs B"), alternatives ("alternatives to B") and best-of lists ("the best tools for C"). If such pages exist on your site — honest, specific and structured — the assistants have something to quote with your name in it.

items.title: Pick an idea
items.text: Seenlab suggests pages from the competitors the assistants recommend most and from your main prompt. You can also write your own.

items.title: Choose the language
items.text: The language of the site and of the customers who will read it.

items.title: Edit and publish
items.text: Check every fact about competitors, add real screenshots or numbers, publish at a clean address and paste the FAQ schema.

items.title: Make it findable
items.text: Link it from the home page or a hub page, send it with IndexNow (SEO page) and log an experiment.

blocks.text: Be fair. A comparison that only praises you is ignored by readers and assistants alike. Say who each option is best for — including when it is not you.
Changes lists what moved since the previous measurement, per prompt and assistant: a mention lost or gained, a place up or down. It is the list to check each morning.

An experiment is something you did to be recommended more — a comparison page, a guest article, getting listed on a review site, a forum answer. Log the day; Seenlab compares the mention rate across all prompts in the 14 days before with the days from 2 to 16 after.
Assistants that search the web react in days; memory-based ones in weeks or months. Judge an experiment on the web-search assistants first.
Seenlab counts a mention when an answer uses any of your names: the full product name, the short name, your domain, and any alias you add (an old name, the company name, a common misspelling).

items: Add every name customers actually use.
Your website is what Seenlab uses to recognize your own pages among the sources.
Product facts are what answers are checked against (see "Accuracy and positioning").
